column2: How do I note that a page is in Latin, and use a register’s table (or index)?
column3: Language: each page takes the collection’s language (“Edit” → “🏛 Where it is, who can see it” → Language), but it can have its own: on the page, “🔤 Language” → “✎ Change…”, or several at once in the “🗂 Status” tab (“☑ Choose pages” → “⋯ More” → “Language of these pages…”). When a page’s text looks like Latin, the app suggests “Note “Latin””. In the Status tab, “🔤 Language: Latin” shows only those pages, and “What’s left” says “including Latin: p. …”. Tables: mark the page “📇 Table or index” (on the page: “📄 Page type”, or “⋯ More” in the Status tab), then make its “📊 Page table”: one row per entry (name, year…) and one column for the reference (“f° 12”, “p. 3”). In the “📑 Table of contents” tab, “📇 Tables and indexes” gathers all the entries: a click takes you to the page referred to, and the app flags what the table refers to but is missing (absent page, or no page with that name). You can search it for a name. Covers, flyleaves and appendices are marked the same way.
